PullRequest.Title: Add Copy button design guidance
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- Add standalone draft guidance for CopyButton and CopyFeedback, including success, failure, accessibility, API, and fixture details.
- Register the component and its fixture under Components > Primitives, and keep the generic Button page concise with a cross-link.

## Issues addressed

| Severity | Issue | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| Medium | The curated fixture path did not match Component Explorer's exported group path. | Register the actual `base/copyButton/CopyButton` group; portable export now includes all four theme variants. |
| Low | Markdown syntax in the preview description was rendered literally. | Use plain text for the preview description; the rendered page now displays the fixture caption cleanly. |

| `node /tmp/vscode-design-system-copy-button/scripts/export.mjs /Users/leemurray/.copilot/session-state/099cb8d1-e000-4d19-8e94-1f6be0f59d62/files/copy-button-pr/after-copy-button.html --root /Users/leemurray/Documents/WORK/D3/VS_CODE/vscode.worktrees/copy-button-design-guidance --guidance-only` | Passed; exported 53 topics, 43 documents, and 92 fixture variants. |

The same suite passes 177/177 against the unchanged base. |

## Review status

- Unresolved actionable findings in the product diff: None
- Residual risks: The latest viewer's three fixed-inventory assertions need a separate viewer-repository update; product validation, focused viewer validation, and portable export pass.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: discoverDesignSpecs finishes its existing directory scans and sequential front-matter reads, then checkComponentCuration validates registered design/owner paths before validation returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Scan existing roots and open/read/close each design specification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same three recursive root scans; one additional specification open/read/close per invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same scans and reads of all other specifications, without the new Copy button document.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The additional small file read completes before discovery returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve and stat the design document and implementation owner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two additional checkFile calls, each performing realpath and stat, per validation invocation; curation.json is still read once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Copy button curation entry; all other curation checks and the single JSON read already occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A fixed number of checks is awaited before validation returns.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One additional 32-line specification and one curation entry; existing repository-wide scan roots are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing sequential spec reads and sequential curation checks; no new parallel fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application-level discovery cache; each invocation rereads specifications. The new front matter fits in one 4096-byte read. Warm filesystem caching does not change call counts.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected complete diffs and the validator's discovery and curation loops.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem latency varies; the added work is bounded to one small document and two path checks.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable regression: normal bounded content-validation work, without increased scanning scope or multiplicative calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Build or export the design-system book with the newly registered component
Scenarios.CriticalPath: validateDesignSystem optionally awaits the external viewer's validation, listing, and export commands; exported output is read before the command succeeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run git log and the selected viewer's validate/list/export CLIs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged: one git command, one viewer validation command when selected, and two additional viewer commands for full export.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Exactly the same wrapper command count and ordering, with one fewer registered chapter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing synchronous commands gate completion of the developer-invoked validation/export workflow, not editor startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read viewer package metadata, prepare export output, and read the generated HTML snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged wrapper-level operations; output gains the new chapter and associated fixture content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same metadata/output operations and snapshot read, with a smaller content inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing metadata/output work gates CLI completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One new component chapter selecting one existing fixture group, three owner files, and seven API members.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing execFileSync calls remain serialized: git identity, viewer validate, and, for full export, viewer list and export. No new subprocess loop is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The repository wrapper has no cross-command viewer cache. Viewer-internal source caching and rendered-page scheduling are outside this checkout and cannot be established.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for unchanged subprocess count and bounded metadata addition; external viewer implementation is unavailable.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cannot establish exact external viewer source-read counts, cache behavior, output size, or rendering duration from this repository.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression. Additional requested chapter content alone does not establish an expensive scheduling or scaling change.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render the Copy button preview or export its theme variants
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing fixture infrastructure awaits theme/style setup and syntax-highlighting registration, then renders three button states. The fixture uses a no-op copy callback rather than a real clipboard write.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the default file-icon theme JSON; color themes are supplied by imported modules.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced icon-theme load per document/theme object across fixtures, not three calls per button or four duplicate concurrent theme loads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same boundary and cache in the existing CopyButton fixture and other component fixtures; registration now selects this existing group for the curated book.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold preview readiness waits for theme initialization; warm variants reuse the promise.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read external stylesheet text for shared fixture CSS initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one fetch per external stylesheet during the single shared bundle initialization per document; inline styles need no fetch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same shared setup already ran for existing component previews.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial fixture style setup awaits the shared bundle; subsequent variants reuse it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load Oniguruma WASM and syntax grammar resources through asynchronous XHR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared WASM load per document and a bounded grammar set for existing fixture languages per tokenizer initialization; overlapping fixtures share one initialization. No calls originate from the three copy-button states.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The CopyButton fixture already used the same generic setup. The PR adds its curated-book association without changing setup, grammar cardinality, or resource loading.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing generic fixture readiness awaits this setup before invoking renderCopyButtons.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One existing fixture group expands to four themes: dark, light, dark high contrast, and light high contrast. Each rendered variant contains exactly three buttons.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Theme setup uses existing Promise.all; grammar loading uses the existing fixed language set. Concurrent live fixtures share initialization promises. External export scheduling is unavailable; the PR does not change fixture concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Color-theme promises are coalesced by theme object and use imported JSON; file-icon loading is coalesced by icon-theme object. Stylesheet bundle loading is shared once per document. Tokenizer setup is shared while fixtures retain references; its grammar state is disposed at zero references, and the WASM promise remains shared. Cold failures do not introduce a new retry loop.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced fixture theme expansion, its fixed three-state loop, shared loading promises, syntax initialization, and disposable ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual additional export cost depends on whether the external viewer renders fixtures or reuses artifacts and whether variants share a browser document; those implementation details are not present.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: bounded preview content uses existing coalesced infrastructure, and buttons/feedback are owned by the fixture disposable store.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use CopyButton and CopyFeedback in the editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Unchanged CopyButton.copy awaits its supplied copy callback before showing feedback; the PR changes guidance and catalog metadata only.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing user copy activations; no new runtime caller, listener, timer loop, or retained collection is added.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing callback and feedback scheduling are unchanged; design documents and curation add no runtime concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Runtime cache behavior is unchanged; repeated successful feedback uses the existing reset scheduler.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: no executable product code changes, and both implementation files are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression or concrete performance-regression fix in the product runtime.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all four changed files and every diff page against base 0a4b87572487af43f21427c0aa781ee408a16d27. Traced validation, viewer subprocess orchestration, fixture expansion, resource-loading caches, and cleanup. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issues or concrete regression fixes found. External viewer internals were unavailable; review was read-only and static.
